name: spec
description: Spec pipeline v7 — a small code program run by a trusted engineer, verified by executed evidence. Lifecycle: /spec:genesis (greenfield) → roadmap briefs → /spec:sketch → /spec:plan → /spec:run (design when due, then build, then review, each driver-stepped with one fresh-context reviewer and a derived verdict) → /spec:release; plus /spec:atlas, /spec:status, /spec:doctor, /spec:enforce, /spec:escape, /spec:replay. Changelog (last 3): 7.125.0 — Soft reviewer findings are now advisory: verdict.js's disposition pool holds only hard survivors plus leg findings, so a soft-only reviewer return derives CLEAN with zero dispositions instead of demanding a fix/waive/reject cycle, and the review driver self-dispositions an empty hard pool straight to CLOSE with no DISPOSITIONS mark required; `--mark dispositions --file` now derives the waived/rejected/fix-dispatched tallies from the disposer return itself, with the count flags becoming an optional cross-check rather than a hand-typed requirement. 7.124.0 — review-legs.js sets SPEC_REVIEW_BASE in every leg subprocess's environment so a host check running inside the gate or suite leg can judge against the base this review is actually judging rather than a merge-base it re-derives from branch topology (which collapses onto the wrong commit once a branch has merged); plugin-bump.js resolveBase() honors it as a 40-hex-only candidate ahead of main/origin-main. replay.js's --record cross-checks a baseline-red or new pristine-red --legs claim against the cited review run's one CLEAN ledger row instead of trusting the claim on shape alone, and refuses one that row contradicts. replay.md's step 7 rung 3 now resolves a still-red pristine-baseline verification deterministically: a second still-red re-run with the same first failing line records setup-failed with pristine-red:<leg> and stops with its manifests retained, instead of asking the user a question the evidence cannot answer; a different or green result still falls through to the question seam. 7.123.0 — `/spec:mocks` gains a WALK state between WIREFRAMES and SIGNOFF: each declared journey is walked once by a fresh-context critic that reads its screens in declared order, enters their gray empty/loading/error states as branches, and may report only six flow breaks (no-path-back, no-path-forward, dead-end-state, missing-data, ambiguous-control, unrecoverable-error), never naming, hierarchy, density, or a "consider…" suggestion. Findings are mock-scope notes of `kind: "walk"`, cited to a screen and a declared state; `--mark journey-walked --journey <j>` refuses while one is still open, and `--reopen walk:<j>` (plus the journey/shapes cascade) invalidates it. `spec/agents/design-critic.md` is rewritten in place as this one journey-walk critic, replacing the four-heuristic per-screen pass it also ran at `/spec:sketch`'s Critique step; the mocks stage cannot be signed off on a journey nobody walked.
